classes.name: House of Representatives general elections
classes.locator: https://elections.gov.bz/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/Cap-9-Representation-of-the-People-Act.pdf (s. 17: Belize divided into the electoral divisions of the First Schedule; each represented by one elected member)
classes.note: One member per electoral division by first past the post (Representation of the People Act s. 17 (3)): 18 divisions in 1979, 28 in 1984 and 1989, 29 from 1993 to 2003, and 31 since 2008 (Act No. 11 of 2005). The House first sat after the election of 1965 under the self-government constitution of 1964; the Department publishes returns from 1979, and its 1993 and 1998 files are scans without a text layer. Parliament runs five years from its first sitting unless dissolved earlier, so the date is called.

classes.name: City and town council elections (mayors and councillors)
classes.locator: https://elections.gov.bz/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/Chapter-87-Town-Councils-Act.pdf (s. 3 (3): a Mayor and six other members; s. 4: office until the last day of February after two years in office; s. 10: Mayor directly elected)
classes.note: Every city and town council is elected at once: the mayor directly and the other members (ten in Belize City, six elsewhere) at large, each elector voting for up to that many candidates. The Acts of 1999 replaced the Belize City Council Act (Cap. 66) and the Local Government (District Boards) Act (Cap. 67); the first councils under them were elected in March 1999 (Belize City) and March 2000 (Belmopan and the seven towns), all holding office to February 2003, and every council since in the March after two years in office. The Department publishes no 2015 or 2018 results. By-elections fill vacancies within ninety days and count here.

classes.name: Village and community council elections
classes.locator: https://elections.gov.bz/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/Cap-88-Village-Councils-Act.pdf (s. 5: a council holds office for three years; s. 6: seven members elected; s. 3: community councils under the same Parts; s. 35: election regulations by the Elections and Boundaries Commission)
classes.note: Village Councils Act No. 30 of 1999. Each village (and each recognized community) elects a chairperson and six members at large for three years; the Department runs the polls in waves on Sundays from May to July of each cycle year, and declares uncontested councils on nomination day. Its pages list cycles from 2010; the 2010 and 2013 pages hold no files, and per-village sheets start in 2016. By-elections count here.
